title: Uniform sampling by repeated rejection
statement: Let $N\ge 1$ and let $\delta>0$. Set $k=\lceil\log_2\lceil\delta^{-1}\rceil\rceil$ and $m=k\,\mathrm{size}(N-1)$. The algorithm defining uniform sampling is computable in polynomial time; on input the pair encoding of the pair consisting of the binary representation of $N$ followed by $k$ ones, and an arbitrary bit string $r$, it returns the encoding of the result of sampling from $r$ with parameters $N,k$. Every returned value is less than $N$. Under the uniform distribution on bit strings of length $m$, for each $i<N$, the probability of returning $i$, multiplied by $N$, equals one minus the probability of returning no value; moreover, the probability of returning no value is at most $\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a natural number with $1\le N$
For the algorithm identity, $r$ is any bit string
For the range claim, $r$ is any bit string and $i$ is a natural number, with the claim conditional on the sample returning $i$
The sampling probabilities use $m=k\,\mathrm{size}(N-1)$ random bits
